title: Autograd & Optimization
description: Study computational graphs and leaf gradients, gradient accumulation and zeroing, detach, no-grad and evaluation mode, and optimizers, schedules and parameter groups. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Computational graphs and leaf gradients
lessons.description: Derive the gradient of (2x - 1) squared at x = 3, then compare it with an autograd calculation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Autograd records operations performed on tensors that require gradients. Backward applies the chain rule through that graph and accumulates gradients in leaf parameters. The graph reflects the operations actually executed, which makes data-dependent forward paths possible. Gradient recording is different from updating model parameters.
lessons.whyItMatters: Backward computes gradients; the optimizer update is a separate operation.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: For y = 3x squared, dy/dx = 6x. At x = 2 the derivative is 12; an optimizer still needs to use that derivative to change x.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Derive the gradient of (2x - 1) squared at x = 3, then compare it with an autograd calculation. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Backward computes gradients; the optimizer update is a separate operation.
commonMistakes: Calling backward directly performs the optimizer step.

lessons.title: Gradient accumulation and zeroing
lessons.description: Sketch a four-microbatch loop and mark zero_grad, backward, and step. Explain how the schedule changes for ordinary training.
lessons.conceptOverview: Gradients accumulate across backward calls. This supports intentional microbatch accumulation but causes errors when accidental. For equal-sized microbatches, dividing each loss by the accumulation count reproduces the gradient of their mean under the same model state. Unequal microbatches require weighting by example count.
lessons.whyItMatters: Clear once before an accumulation window and step once after its final microbatch.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Gradients accumulate across backward calls. This supports intentional microbatch accumulation but causes errors when accidental. For equal-sized microbatches, dividing each loss by the accumulation count reproduces the gradient of their mean under the same model state. Unequal microbatches require weighting by example count.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Gradients accumulate across backward calls. This supports intentional microbatch accumulation but causes errors when accidental. For equal-sized microbatches, dividing each loss by the accumulation count reproduces the gradient of their mean under the same model state. Unequal microbatches require weighting by example count.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: Four microbatches intended to form one effective batch should trigger one optimizer step. Clearing gradients after each microbatch discards the earlier contributions.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Sketch a four-microbatch loop and mark zero_grad, backward, and step. Explain how the schedule changes for ordinary training. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Clear once before an accumulation window and step once after its final microbatch.
commonMistakes: Clear gradients after every microbatch even when accumulating an effective batch.

lessons.title: Detach, no-grad and evaluation mode
lessons.description: Classify validation, saliency analysis, and a frozen-feature cache by whether they need evaluation mode and gradient recording.
lessons.conceptOverview: Detach cuts a tensor from its recorded history while potentially sharing its storage. A no-grad context prevents recording new operations. Evaluation mode changes behaviors such as dropout and batch normalization; it does not itself turn off autograd. Choose each control for its actual purpose.
lessons.whyItMatters: Evaluation mode and gradient recording are independent controls.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: Validation can use model.eval() together with no-grad. Attribution methods may use evaluation mode while deliberately retaining gradients for input sensitivity analysis.

lessons.title: Optimizers, schedules and parameter groups
lessons.description: Design parameter groups for a backbone and head. Record which parameters are trainable and how learning rates change over epochs.
lessons.conceptOverview: An optimizer maps gradients and optional state into parameter updates. Momentum and adaptive optimizers maintain additional state that matters when resuming training. Parameter groups allow different learning rates or decay policies. Scheduler timing must match the documented update convention rather than being placed arbitrarily.
lessons.whyItMatters: Resume optimizer and scheduler state when continuing the same training trajectory.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A pretrained backbone may use a lower learning rate than a new classifier head. Restoring only weights loses momentum or adaptive state and can change the next update.
